title: The perfect locus with fixed degree
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and let $E\in D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ be
perfect. Given $i,r\in\mathbb{Z}$ there is
an open subscheme $U\subseteq X$ characterized by the property: a
morphism $f:Y\to X$ factors through $U$ if and only if $Lf^*E$ is
isomorphic to a locally free $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module of rank $r$ placed in
degree $i$.

proof.text: If $r<0$, take $U=\varnothing$. Otherwise let $x\in X$. By [def-pc-perfect-complex], on an affine open $\mathrm{Spec}(A)\ni x$ the object $E$ is represented by a bounded complex of finite projective $A$-modules; since it has finitely many terms, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover] applied to each term gives a principal open $\mathrm{Spec}(A_g)\ni x$ on which $E$ is represented by a bounded complex $M^\bullet$ of finite free modules. Over the local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, repeatedly apply [lem-weil-pbc-free-complex-unit-entry-splits] whenever a differential has a unit matrix entry. Each application splits off a contractible two-term identity complex and lowers the sum of the ranks, so the process terminates with a bounded finite-free complex whose differential matrices all lie in the maximal ideal.

The remaining differential becomes zero after tensoring with the residue field because all its entries lie in the maximal ideal. Hence its fibre cohomology is the remaining graded vector space. If the fibre cohomology is zero outside degree $i$ and has dimension $r$ in degree $i$, the remaining free terms have rank zero outside degree $i$ and rank $r$ in degree $i$. The finitely many basis changes and inverses used above are defined on an open neighbourhood of $x$, where $E$ is therefore quasi-isomorphic to $\mathcal O^{\oplus r}[-i]$.

Define $U$ to be the set of points satisfying the residue-field cohomology condition. The neighbourhood construction in the preceding step shows that $U$ is open and that $E|_U$ is locally a free rank-$r$ module in degree $i$. On overlaps these descriptions agree through the cohomology sheaf $H^i(E)|_U$, so $H^i(E)|_U$ is locally free of rank $r$ and $E|_U\simeq H^i(E)|_U[-i]$.

If $f:Y\to X$ factors through $U$, the local finite-free descriptions pull back term by term by [lem-pc-flat-complex-derived-pullback] and show that $Lf^*E$ has the required form. Conversely, suppose $Lf^*E$ has that form, let $y\in Y$ with image $x$, and let $j_y:\mathrm{Spec}\,\kappa(y)\to Y$, $j_x:\mathrm{Spec}\,\kappa(x)\to X$ be the canonical morphisms, so $f\circ j_y=j_x\circ(\mathrm{Spec}\,\kappa(y)\to\mathrm{Spec}\,\kappa(x))$. By [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition], $Lj_y^*Lf^*E\cong L(\mathrm{Spec}\,\kappa(y)\to\mathrm{Spec}\,\kappa(x))^*Lj_x^*E$. Computing both sides with the local finite-free representative $M^\bullet$ of $E$ near $x$ (a bounded complex of flat modules, so pulled back term by term by [lem-pc-flat-complex-derived-pullback], with [def-pc-derived-pullback]), the derived fibre of $Lf^*E$ at $y$ is $(M^\bullet\otimes\kappa(x))\otimes_{\kappa(x)}\kappa(y)$, while that of $L[-i]$ ($L$ locally free of rank $r$) is $\kappa(y)^{r}$ in degree $i$. A field extension is faithfully flat, and the scalar-extension dimension formula [lem-pc-finrank-field-base-change] preserves the vanishing and dimension of the finite-dimensional fibre cohomology. Thus $x$ satisfies the defining condition of $U$; the image of $f$ is contained in $U$, equivalently $f$ factors through the open subscheme $U$.
